spec_match.rationale: The eager-vs-lazy framing (read() returning the type list, per-format data fetched on getType()) matches the change, but the timeline is illustrative prose and the claimed timings are invented rather than measured.

interactive.rationale: No controls. clipboard.read() is present on this engine (probed true) and a real timing comparison — write a multi-format clipboard item, then time read() vs the first getType() — is exactly what this page describes without doing.

blurb_alignment.rationale: 'This comparison shows the timeline difference' — it narrates one; nothing is shown from the visitor's engine.

edge_cases.rationale: No permission handling (clipboard-read requires a grant), no unsupported state, no focus-requirement note — all real hurdles a live version must and should surface.

references.rationale: Feature index links chromestatus; the description cites no spec/design-doc anchors.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite exists; page anchors nothing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP run: navigator.clipboard.read and readText both present (probed); page renders clean — 0px overflow both classes, zero console errors; nothing else to exercise.

openQuestions.title: Measure the lazy read for real
openQuestions.detail: Add a two-button lab: write a multi-format ClipboardItem, then time read() (type list) and the first getType() fetch separately, rendering the visitor's own measured timeline beside the narrated one — with real permission-prompt and focus handling, and honest fallback where the API or grant is unavailable.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Clipboard reads need explicit user action and permission surfacing.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Relevant only to the proposed fix; current page has no interaction at all.

summary: Reviewed headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the change is fully measurable on this very engine (clipboard.read present, probed) yet the page only narrates an invented timeline. Major question filed for a real measured comparison with permission handling.
